ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Year-one academic inquiry, writing and civic engagement.
ACCPPDE101.topics: Scholarly sources and research questions; Argumentation and thesis statements; Literature synthesis; Academic integrity and referencing; Community engagement; Personal learning goals and reflective learning; Collaborative learning; Self-efficacy; Stress and time management; Responsible use of AI
ACCPPDE101.methods: Scholarly literature searching and source evaluation; Literature synthesis; CARS model for research introductions; Reflective development planning; Community project co-design

BENECON111.name: Introduction to Economics
BENECON111.contribution: teaches microeconomics (supply and demand, game theory, consumer behaviour) and macroeconomics; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the economic theory that psychology and economics sets against actual behaviour
BENECON111.topics: Supply and demand; Game theory; Rational consumer choice; Individual and market demand; Production and costs; Perfect competition; Aggregate output; Unemployment and inflation; Goods and financial markets; IS-LM model
BENECON111.methods: Algebraic and graphical economic analysis; Supply-and-demand analysis; Game-theoretic analysis; IS-LM modelling

BENECON212.name: Microeconomics & Behavior
BENECON212.contribution: analyses consumer behaviour, decision making under uncertainty, non-egoistic preferences and cognitive limitations before turning to markets; it makes a specific complementary contribution to psychology and economics
BENECON212.topics: Choice under uncertainty; Non-egoistic preferences; Cognitive limitations; Monopoly; Imperfect competition and strategic behaviour; Labour markets; Capital markets; General equilibrium; Market efficiency; Externalities; Government intervention
BENECON212.methods: Algebraic microeconomic analysis; Graphical economic analysis; Critical evaluation of economic research

BENECON312.name: Econometrics
BENECON312.contribution: teaches ordinary and generalised least squares and instrumental variables with Monte Carlo simulation and an empirical paper; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the causal-inference and prediction methods of empirical behavioural economics
BENECON312.topics: Econometrics supplies tools to analyze data to answer questions of causality and prediction. In this course you learn three estimators—Ordinary Least Squares, Generalized Least Squares, and Instrumental Variables—and three tests—t-test, F-test, and LM-test. Understanding the basic rules of econometrics, particularly the sampling distribution concept, is key, and the course uses Monte Carlo simulations in Stata to visualize it. Tools are applied to estimate economic relationships and make predictions, and students write an empirical paper.

BENECON314.name: Behavioral Economics
BENECON314.contribution: integrates psychological insight into economic theory, with biases, heuristics and framing studied through experiments; it directly implements psychology and economics
BENECON314.topics: This course integrates insights from psychology into economic theory to better understand how people make decisions. Learn how actual behavior deviates from the predictions of traditional economic models due to biases, heuristics, and framing. Through experiments, students will deepen their understanding of decision-making and its implications for economic theory and practice.

BENENTR211.name: Marketing & Consumer Engagement
BENENTR211.contribution: unpacks what drives consumers' behaviour and engagement with brands, including consumer psychology and responsible trust building; it makes a specific complementary contribution as applied consumer psychology
BENENTR211.topics: Strategic marketing planning; Marketing mix; Customer centricity and experience; Consumer journeys; Market research and augmented insights; Brand identity and image; Brand partnerships; Digital and social marketing; Responsible marketing; Consumer psychology; Nudging and framing; Emerging technologies and marketing agility
BENENTR211.methods: Marketing-strategy case analysis; Advertising-campaign analysis; Kapferer brand-identity prism; Brand design; Primary and secondary consumer research; Consumer-journey mapping; Disruption-response planning

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: teaches research design, operationalization, experimental design and sampling together with descriptive and inferential statistics and analysis of variance; it directly implements the first Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules on research methods and statistics
BENGATE102.topics: Scientific inquiry and hypotheses; Operationalization and measurement; Reliability and validity; Survey construction and sampling; Randomized and quasi-experimental designs; Nonexperimental and qualitative research; Descriptive statistics; Sampling distributions and estimation; Hypothesis testing and confidence intervals; Association and regression; Research ethics and anonymous data collection
BENGATE102.methods: Survey design; Probability and nonprobability sampling; Experimental and nonexperimental research design; R and R Commander data analysis; Descriptive statistics and visualization; Scale-reliability analysis; One- and two-sample mean tests; ANOVA; Chi-square tests; Correlation and regression; Empirical data collection and analysis

BENLEAD211.name: Psychology of Leading Under Pressure
BENLEAD211.contribution: Examines emotion regulation, emotional labour, belonging and psychological safety in organisations. It provides a workplace perspective on inclusion and wellbeing.
BENLEAD211.topics: Emotion regulation strategies; Emotional intelligence; Emotional expression and suppression; Emotional labor; Inclusive leadership; Belonging and identity safety; Psychological safety; Ethnic, cultural, sexual and gender minority experiences; Digital emotion regulation; Psychological measurement, reliability and validity; Ethical survey research in diverse populations; Interpretation and limitations of quantitative evidence; Evidence-based leadership recommendations
BENLEAD211.methods: Theory-driven hypothesis formulation; Quantitative survey research; Established psychological measure selection and evaluation; Qualtrics survey construction and piloting; Ethical participant recruitment and original data collection; Codebook development, reverse coding and scale scoring; Data cleaning and missing-data documentation; Descriptive statistics; Reliability analysis; Correlation analysis; Group comparisons; Introductory multiple regression in SPSS or RStudio; APA-style empirical reporting

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: examines the psychological, social and structural dynamics of organisations (motivation, personality, perception, decision making, group behaviour, leadership and organisational culture); it directly implements work and organisational psychology
BENLEAD311.topics: Diversity, equity and inclusion; Job attitudes and satisfaction; Emotions, stress and workplace health; Personality and individual differences; Perception and decision-making; Motivation; Group behaviour and work teams; Human resource systems; Communication, conflict and negotiation; Leadership, power and politics; Organizational structure; Organizational culture and change
BENLEAD311.methods: Organizational case analysis; Research design and hypothesis formulation; Systematic literature review; PRISMA flow diagrams and checklists; Database searching and study screening; Source-quality appraisal and evidence synthesis

BENLEAD312.name: Negotiation & Strategic Thinking
BENLEAD312.contribution: teaches negotiation and persuasion through simulations and role-plays; it makes a specific complementary contribution as applied interpersonal decision making and conflict management in organisations
BENLEAD312.topics: Interests versus positions; BATNA and ZOPA; Mutual gains and objective criteria; Dual-concern model; Anchoring, framing and concessions; Trade-offs and logrolling; Cognitive biases and influence; Power and emotions; Trust, reputation and ethics; Cross-cultural and organizational negotiation; Negotiation implementation and withdrawal; Stakeholder interests
BENLEAD312.methods: BATNA and ZOPA analysis; Stakeholder-interest mapping; Interest-based negotiation; Negotiation simulations; Narrative and film analysis of bargaining; Negotiation-scene scripting and annotation; Scenario design and reflective evaluation

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: examines AI ethics and the psychology of AI, including over-trust in and resistance to AI in decision making, empathy and attachment to AI companions and algorithmic bias; it directly implements the question of how digital technology changes human behaviour
DISARIN111.topics: Algorithmic fairness and bias; Privacy and surveillance; Responsibility and accountability; Human-value alignment; Moral status of AI; Existential risk and democratic implications; Trust and agency in human-AI interaction; AI in clinical care; Child development and AI; Social and organizational effects of AI; AI in forensic psychology; Cognitive and socioemotional development; AI consciousness and sentience
DISARIN111.methods: Ethical-framework application; Philosophical argument evaluation; Psychological-literature synthesis; Theory-based analysis of AI applications; Research podcast scripting, recording and editing

DISARIN211.name: Decision-making in AI
DISARIN211.contribution: teaches planning and decision making under uncertainty and partial observability; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the formal decision-making methods of the engineering and data-science neighbour of psychology
DISARIN211.topics: Conditional probability, independence and Bayes' rule; Bayesian networks; Temporal probabilistic models; Hidden Markov models and dynamic Bayesian networks; Expected utility; Markov and partially observable decision processes; Exploration-exploitation trade-offs and bandits; Competitive and cooperative multi-agent interaction; Negotiation, auctions and voting; Probabilistic programming
DISARIN211.methods: Probabilistic inference; Bayesian-network modelling; Temporal probabilistic modelling; Expected-utility analysis; Sequential decision modelling; Game-theoretic analysis; Probabilistic programming

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: teaches data cleaning, manipulation and visualisation with hands-on work on social-science data sets and ends with an own research project; it directly implements the data-handling and analysis skills that the scientific-inquiry modules develop in scripts
DISDATA111.topics: Data visualization; Exploratory data analysis; Tidy data; Data transformation and integration; Dates and times; Web data; Text data; Geospatial data; Programming functions; Data-based research questions
DISDATA111.methods: R programming; ggplot visualization and grammar of graphics; Data cleaning, tidying and transformation; Data import and joins; Web scraping; Text-data analysis; Geospatial-data analysis

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: teaches regression, classification, resampling and clustering for understanding data and predicting outcomes; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the data-analysis and prediction methods that the course catalogue says rest on programming in modern behavioural neuroscience
DISDATA211.topics: Prediction and model accuracy; Regression and classification; Resampling and validation; Model selection and regularization; High-dimensional data; Nonlinear regression; Tree-based learning; Support vector methods; Dimension reduction; Unsupervised learning; Feature engineering
DISDATA211.methods: Linear and logistic regression; Generative classification; Cross-validation and bootstrap; Subset selection; Ridge regression and LASSO; Splines and generalized additive models; Basic and advanced decision-tree methods; Support vector machines; Principal component analysis; Clustering; Predictive-performance evaluation; R or Python implementation

DISGATE101.name: Introduction to Programming
DISGATE101.contribution: teaches structured and object-oriented programming in Python with testing and debugging; it directly implements the procedural programming and algorithmic thinking that Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking IV teaches in Python
DISGATE101.topics: Python language fundamentals; Strings and input/output; Branching and loops; Functions; Tuples, lists, sets and dictionaries; Aliasing and cloning; Recursion; Exceptions and assertions; Object-oriented programming; Inheritance; Computational problem-solving
DISGATE101.methods: Structured programming in Python; Object-oriented programming; Recursive problem-solving; Program tracing; Testing and debugging; Exception handling

ENSSUST111.name: Climate Change
ENSSUST111.contribution: examines the drivers of anthropogenic climate change, its impacts on natural systems and the societal transformations it drives; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the climate challenge that the programme names as a problem psychologists help address
ENSSUST111.topics: Anthropogenic climate change; Greenhouse gases; Feedback loops and tipping points; Ocean acidification and sea-level rise; Biosphere impacts; Agriculture, transport and construction; Climate and health; Climate justice and governance; Paris Agreement; Renewable energy and sustainable heat; Carbon removal and geoengineering; Climate communication and misinformation; Climate anxiety; Mitigation and adaptation
ENSSUST111.methods: Stakeholder interviewing; Short-film production for climate communication; Source-credibility evaluation; What? So What? Now What? reflective model

ENSSUST113.name: Calling Bullshit
ENSSUST113.contribution: teaches how cognitive biases and social pressures make people vulnerable to misinformation and how to evaluate claims and scientific credibility; it directly implements the critical-thinking strand of Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking I, which addresses biases, fallacies and illusions
ENSSUST113.topics: Bullshit, lying and misinformation; Historical hoaxes and propaganda; Cognitive bias and motivated reasoning; Social identity and information overload; Scientific credibility and pseudoscience; Publication bias and misconduct; Misleading statistics and data displays; Reasoning fallacies; Deepfakes; Misinformation diffusion; Debunking and counter-narratives; Medical and climate misinformation
ENSSUST113.methods: Source-credibility evaluation; Fact-checking protocols; Reasoning-fallacy detection; Critical analysis of statistical claims; Misinformation-network mapping; Deepfake video construction and analysis; Debunking-message design; Expert interviewing; Documentary-style explanatory video production

GOSGATE102.name: Law, Society & Justice
GOSGATE102.contribution: offers legal, social and normative perspectives on law, from constitutional and criminal law to human rights; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice question and to the law that the transdisciplinary specialisation connects with psychology
GOSGATE102.topics: Legal positivism and empirical and normative perspectives; Common-law and civil-law traditions; Constitutional and administrative law; Criminal law; International law and human rights; Property, contract and tort law; Justice; Law and social control; Law and social change; Race and gender in law; Family law
GOSGATE102.methods: Legal interpretation; Case-law research and IRAC case briefing; Demand-letter drafting; Mock-trial legal argumentation; Socio-legal research design; Literature review

GOSLAWJ111.name: Human Rights: Law & Philosophy
GOSLAWJ111.contribution: studies human rights as positive law, history and philosophy; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice and inclusion challenges the programme names
GOSLAWJ111.topics: Human-rights generations and justifications; UDHR and its formation; UN and European human-rights protection; Natural law and natural rights; Legal positivism and cultural relativism; Universality and statelessness; Human dignity; Right to life and reproductive rights; Torture and punishment; Freedom of religion; Freedom of expression; Democracy
GOSLAWJ111.methods: Treaty and legal-text analysis; Judicial and treaty-body case-law research; Case-law analysis; Philosophical text and argument analysis

GOSLAWJ211.name: Criminal Law & Criminal Justice
GOSLAWJ211.contribution: teaches criminal accountability, guilt, justification and excuse and the presumption of innocence; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the criminal-law framework with which legal psychology works
GOSLAWJ211.topics: Criminal accountability; Actus reus and causation; Intent, recklessness and negligence; Legality and presumption of innocence; Theories of punishment; Criminalization and its limits; Justifications and excuses; Preparation and attempt; Participation in crime; Corporate criminal liability; Criminology and organized crime
GOSLAWJ211.methods: Comparative criminal-law analysis; Case-law analysis; Application of legal principles to hypothetical facts; Legal-advice memorandum writing; Simulated legal-aid argumentation; Criminological research design and literature review

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: asks what consciousness is, whether the mind can be explained neurobiologically and whether artificial systems can be conscious; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the foundational debates about the mind that the Mind core module addresses
GOSPHIL214.topics: Persons and personal identity; Psychological and narrative theories of identity; Buddhist non-self; Split-brain cases and self-knowledge; Behaviourism; Physicalism and functionalism; Mind-body problem; Content externalism and internalism; AI intelligence and consciousness; Virtual reality; Dreaming and perception; Transformative experience; Value of conscious experience; Animal minds
GOSPHIL214.methods: Close philosophical reading; Conceptual analysis; Reconstruction and evaluation of arguments; Comparison of theories of mind; Literature-based philosophical research

GOSPOLI112.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
GOSPOLI112.contribution: gives the analytical tools to compare political systems and explain growing dissatisfaction and support for parties at the political extremes; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the political dimension of polarisation and of psychology and politics
GOSPOLI112.topics: Democracy and authoritarianism; Democratization and democratic backsliding; States, nations and nationalism; Constitutions and courts; Executives, legislatures and bureaucracies; Political economy; Parties and party systems; Populism and technocracy; Elections and electoral systems; Political culture and polarization; Political participation; Interest groups and public policy
GOSPOLI112.methods: Theory-driven qualitative and quantitative research; Concept operationalization and democracy measurement; V-Dem data analysis; Comparative case analysis; Academic literature searching with OpenAlex and AI tools; Empirical election analysis; Research-question formulation

GOSPOLI313.name: Peace & Conflict
GOSPOLI313.contribution: examines theories of conflict and peacebuilding drawing on sociology, political science and law; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the study of social division and polarisation
GOSPOLI313.topics: Conflict theories and structural violence; Identity and historical grievances; Colonialism and forced migration; International peace and security; Humanitarian law and human rights; Positive, negative and hybrid peace; Local peacebuilding; Frozen conflicts; Counterterrorism and rule of law; Transitional justice; Gender and conflict; Development and peacebuilding; Reconciliation, arts and religion; Global South perspectives; Travelling concepts and researcher positionality
GOSPOLI313.methods: Interdisciplinary Research Process; Cross-disciplinary travelling-concept analysis; Conflict case analysis; Context and stakeholder mapping; Annotated bibliography and evidence synthesis; Policy-option appraisal; Policy-brief and background-dossier development; Researcher positionality analysis; Comparative research podcast production

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: teaches sociological concepts, methods and theories for analysing everyday interaction, institutions and social structure; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the social-structural perspective that the transdisciplinary specialisation combines with psychology
GOSSOCI111.topics: Sociological imagination and knowledge; Social structure and socialization; Classical social theory; Colonialism and the formation of sociology; Solidarity and modernity; Identity, belonging and othering; Groups and social networks; Capital, class and mobility; Race and gender inequality; Global inequality and migration; Education and labour-market inequality
GOSSOCI111.methods: Theory-guided sociological case analysis; Comparative analysis of sociological perspectives; Library-based social-science research; Sociological research-question formulation

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: teaches the design, data collection, analysis and interpretation of qualitative research on how people make sense of social processes; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the method for studying societal problems that quantitative methods do not capture
GOSSOCI212.topics: Qualitative knowledge and research design; Ethics, positionality and reflexivity; Mixed methods; Participatory research; Interview and focus-group approaches; Ethnography and participant observation; Documentary and archival sources; Visual and participatory media; Coding and thematic interpretation; Qualitative research dissemination
GOSSOCI212.methods: Qualitative research design; Interviews; Focus groups; Ethnography and participant observation; Documentary and archival analysis; Visual-data analysis; Participatory video and drawing; Transcription; Qualitative coding; Thematic analysis; NVivo-supported analysis; Reflexive methodological evaluation

GOSSOCI215.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
GOSSOCI215.contribution: studies social-movement theories and environmental justice with feminist, anti-colonial and degrowth perspectives and civic engagement; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the social-justice and climate questions
GOSSOCI215.topics: Focuses on social movement theories and environmental justice. Uses case studies from the Environmental Justice Atlas and integrates perspectives such as feminism, anti‑colonialism, degrowth and environmental peacebuilding to encourage civic engagement.

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: examines civil society, solidarity, social capital and social trust; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the questions of social connection and social division
GOSSOCI311.topics: Civil society; Social trust and social capital; Hegemony; Critical theory; Public spheres, digital publics and counterpublics; Solidarity and civil repair; Civil sphere; Social movements and intersectionality; Migrant solidarity; Civil society under authoritarianism; Decolonial critique; Public sociology
GOSSOCI311.methods: Comparative social-theory analysis; Theory-guided empirical case analysis; Document and secondary-source analysis; Structured reflection on civil-society engagement or observation; Sociological research design

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: Uses study designs, confounding, association and causal reasoning to investigate disease patterns and appraise population-health evidence. This complements experimental psychology with observational study methods.
HCBBIOM111.topics: Disease frequency and risk; Incidence and prevalence; Measures of association; Epidemiological study designs; Bias, confounding and causality; Outbreak investigation; Social and environmental health determinants; Health inequalities; Health promotion; Health-needs assessment; Screening; Evidence-informed interventions and implementation
HCBBIOM111.methods: Epidemiological rate and risk calculation; Descriptive and analytic epidemiology; Study-design and evidence appraisal; Population-health data interpretation; Outbreak analysis; Health-needs assessment; Stakeholder interviewing; Evidence-informed intervention development

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: teaches the principles of pharmacology, drug targets, pharmacokinetics and the neuronal, hormonal and cellular regulation that drugs affect; it makes a specific complementary contribution to psychopharmacology as a general pharmacology course rather than a course on psychoactive drugs
HCBBIOM311.topics: Drug discovery and targets; Drug-receptor interactions; Pharmacodynamics; Absorption, distribution, metabolism and elimination; Pharmacokinetics; Antimicrobial therapy; Inflammation and immunopharmacology; Autonomic regulation; Neurotransmission and psychoactive drugs; Pharmacogenomics; Drug toxicity; Access to experimental treatments and evidence; Homeopathy
HCBBIOM311.methods: Concentration-response modelling; Pharmacokinetic time-concentration and time-response analysis; Pharmacodynamic and pharmacokinetic parameter calculation; Virtual organ-bath experiments; Hypothesis and experimental-design development

HCBBIOM313.name: Mechanisms of Disease
HCBBIOM313.contribution: relates normal function and pathophysiology for six organ systems including the central nervous system; it makes a specific complementary contribution to the neurological side of neuropsychology, without covering psychiatric disorders
HCBBIOM313.topics: Organ-system disease mechanisms; Nutrition and digestive disease; Hematological and cardiovascular disease; Respiratory disease; Renal failure, dialysis and transplantation; Endocrine disorders; Neurological disease; Etiology and pathogenesis; Diagnosis, treatment and prognosis; Medical ethics; Rheumatic disease
HCBBIOM313.methods: Clinical case analysis; Differential diagnosis reasoning; Critical appraisal of diagnostic and laboratory procedures; Integration of anatomy, physiology and clinical evidence; Mechanistic modelling of an imaginary disease; Biomedical literature comparison

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: studies the evolution of brains, brain regions and rhythms that regulate behaviour, animal models, research ethics and disorders, with laboratory work; it directly implements the biological and neuroscientific side of Brain and Cognition
HCBCOGN112.topics: Nervous-system evolution and comparative anatomy; Brain cells and morphology; Cerebral circulation and nerves; Animal behaviour and welfare; Sentience and research ethics; Reduction, refinement and replacement; Enrichment and brain development; Regulatory and sexual behaviour; Lifestyle drugs; Circadian rhythms and sleep; Sleeping and eating disorders; Depression and anxiety; Gut-brain axis; Hypothalamus and pineal gland; Dying brain and consciousness
HCBCOGN112.methods: Comparative brain-anatomy analysis; Introductory microscopy and cell staining; Brain-model comparison; Ethical appraisal of animal research and the 3Rs; Literature-based analysis of neurobiological disorders

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: examines the neural mechanisms of perception and action and uses methods of cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology; it directly implements the perception and action themes of the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation
HCBCOGN212.topics: Explores neural mechanisms behind perception and action. Examines how the brain processes sensory information and guides goal‑directed behaviour using methods from cognitive neuroscience and neuropsychology.

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: treats memory, attention, emotion, social cognition, consciousness and decision making in depth with neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and experimental approaches; it directly implements learning, memory and attention in the Brain, Cognition and Behaviour specialisation
HCBCOGN311.topics: Neurotransmission and psychoactive drugs; Brain structure and hemispheric specialization; Attention and attentional blink; Memory and long-term potentiation; Emotion; Cognitive control and executive functions; Social cognition; Pain; Consciousness; Brain-behaviour relationships; Neuroscience research ethics
HCBCOGN311.methods: Cognitive-neuroscience experimental design; Attentional-blink experiment; Critical analysis of scientific literature and empirical data; Research-proposal development; Scientific peer review

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: studies the neuroscience and psychology of language comprehension, production, impairment and acquisition with hands-on experiments; it directly implements the language processing that Brain and Cognition lists among the cognitive functions
HCBCOGN312.topics: Psycholinguistics is the study of the neurobiological and psychological factors that enable us to acquire, use, and understand language. Modern research draws on cognitive psychology, neuroscience, and computer science to investigate how language is processed. The course focuses primarily, though not exclusively, on the neuroscience of language. Students examine theoretical and experimental issues in speech production and comprehension, language impairments, the relationship between thought and language, and the evolution and acquisition of language. They also gain hands-on experience with experimental approaches to the study of language and develop an understanding of human linguistic capacity as a subject of multidisciplinary research. Topics covered: What is language? Evolutionary aspects of language and animal communication; language and thought; aphasia; language acquisition; bilingualism; speech comprehension; semantics; reading and dyslexia; speech production.

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: teaches cell biology, molecular biology, cellular physiology and communication and genetics and evolution, with a research-presentation assignment; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the cellular and genetic foundation of the biology of behaviour, and it is the formal prerequisite for the pharmacology, physiology and disease-mechanisms courses of this programme
HCBGATE101.topics: Biological molecules and chemistry of life; Cells, organelles and membranes; Cellular communication; Enzymes and energy metabolism; Cell cycle and division; DNA and heredity; Gene mutation and molecular medicine; Gene-expression regulation and epigenetics; Genomes; Recombinant DNA and biotechnology
HCBGATE101.methods: Scientific-literature searching and synthesis; Analysis of published biological experiments

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces the psychological and neuroscientific study of why people behave as they do, with brain areas, neuronal communication, brain injury and the interplay of nature and nurture; it directly implements the broad introduction to psychology from biological, individual and social perspectives
HCBGATE102.topics: Brain and behaviour; Neural signalling and action potentials; Functional neuroanatomy; Brain development and hemispheric specialization; Associative, non-associative and social learning; Intelligence; Personality and self-concepts; Social influence; Mental disorders and DSM-5-TR; Psychological treatment; Neuroimaging, electrophysiology and converging methods
HCBGATE102.methods: Psychological and neuroscientific research appraisal; Interdisciplinary case-study analysis

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: teaches the normal function of organ systems, including the nervous and endocrine systems, homeostasis and cell signalling; it makes a specific complementary contribution as the physiological basis of biopsychology
HCBLIFE212.topics: Cells, tissues and membrane dynamics; Homeostasis and control; Cellular signalling; Endocrine and nervous regulation; Muscles and movement; Breathing and gas exchange; Blood and cardiovascular function; Renal function; Fluid and electrolyte balance; Digestion and metabolism; Growth and exercise physiology; Reproduction and development
HCBLIFE212.methods: Physiological literature review; Medline/PubMed literature searching; Scientific peer review and evidence-based revision

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: covers the main theories and findings of social psychology (social cognition, attitudes, groups, interpersonal behaviour and social influence); it directly implements the social-psychological strand of Individuals in Context
HCBPSYC111.topics: Social cognition and person perception; The self and self-motives; Social influence; Persuasion, attitudes and behaviour; Group processes; Prejudice, stereotyping and discrimination; Prejudice reduction; Interpersonal aggression; Prosocial behaviour; Interpersonal attraction and close relationships
HCBPSYC111.methods: Critical appraisal of empirical social-psychology research; Literature synthesis; Theory-guided hypothesis formulation; Research design for a proposed social-psychology study

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: teaches multivariate models (linear regression, ANOVA and ANCOVA, factor analysis, logistic regression) and non-parametric tests with experimental methods; it directly implements the statistical analysis of experimental designs and the factor analysis of the Scientific Inquiry & Critical Thinking modules
HCBPSYC211.topics: Experimental, nonexperimental and quasi-experimental designs; Statistical inference; Correlation and regression; Model assumptions and diagnostics; Group comparisons; Covariate adjustment; Factorial, repeated-measures and mixed designs; Categorical outcomes; Latent constructs and scale reliability; Effect size and power; Statistical reporting
HCBPSYC211.methods: R and R Commander data analysis; Multiple linear regression and dummy coding; Regression diagnostics; t-tests and nonparametric alternatives; ANOVA and ANCOVA; Factorial, repeated-measures and mixed-design ANOVA; Logistic regression; Exploratory factor analysis; Principal component analysis; Cronbach's alpha; APA statistical reporting

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: covers mental disorders across the lifespan from a bio-psycho-social perspective, including prevalence, assessment, diagnosis, classification and treatment; it directly implements the clinical conditions that Lifespan Psychology addresses
HCBPSYC212.topics: Mental-disorder concepts and stigma; Historical and contemporary psychopathology; Biopsychosocial causation; Clinical assessment and diagnostic classification; Stress and health; Anxiety and obsessive-compulsive disorders; Mood disorders; Somatic and dissociative disorders; Psychotic disorders; Eating and personality disorders; Substance-related and neurocognitive disorders; Sexuality and mental health; Childhood and adolescent disorders; Forensic psychology; Culture and emotion regulation
HCBPSYC212.methods: Diagnostic case analysis; Application and critique of DSM criteria; Biopsychosocial case formulation; Structured literature searching and screening; Source-quality appraisal; Evidence synthesis; Critical evaluation of etiological and intervention models

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines the bio-psycho-social interplay in health and illness and psychological interventions in medical settings; it makes a specific complementary contribution as clinical health psychology applied to the programme's clinical conditions
HCBPSYC311.topics: Biopsychosocial model; Health inequalities; Health-risk and protective behaviours; Behaviour-change models; Prevention; Stress and coping; Symptom perception; Somatic symptom disorders; Medical consultation; Shared decision-making; Doctor–patient communication; Pain; Chronic illness; Family and caregiver experiences; Quality of life; Cultural competence; Support for healthcare professionals
HCBPSYC311.methods: Psychological case-study analysis; Critical appraisal of health-psychology research and interventions; Clinical-health case formulation; Interviewing-skills practice; Cultural Formulation Interview analysis

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: teaches clinical psychological assessment, psychodiagnostics with its ethical issues and the main psychotherapy approaches; it directly implements the psychodiagnostic strand of the programme
HCBPSYC312.topics: Clinical attitude and ethics; Diagnostic classification; Reliability and validity; Clinical interviews; Personality inventories and projective techniques; Cognitive and neuropsychological assessment; Behavioural and biological assessment; Psychological reporting; Psychodynamic and behavioural therapies; Cognitive therapy and CBT; Person-centered and family therapies; Integrative psychotherapy; Treatment outcomes and evidence; Child and adolescent clinical psychology
HCBPSYC312.methods: Clinical interviewing practice; Introductory psychological-test administration, scoring and interpretation; Psychometric appraisal; Behavioural observation; Integration of assessment data; Psychodiagnostic report writing; Clinical case and therapy-session analysis; Reflective monitoring of clinical skills

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: teaches systematic reviews and meta-analysis with hands-on analysis in R; it makes a specific complementary contribution as research synthesis and statistical scripting for psychological research
HCBPSYC313.topics: Systematic-review purpose and limitations; Review protocols and scope; Literature searching and inclusion criteria; Data extraction and study coding; Risk of bias; Effect-size types and transformations; Fixed- and random-effects models; Effect heterogeneity; Moderators and subgroup differences; Meta-regression; Publication bias; Research synthesis and reporting

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: examines physical, cognitive, social and emotional development from pregnancy to older age, including attachment and some assessment and intervention; it directly implements lifespan psychology
HCBPSYC314.topics: Developmental theories; Genetics and environment; Prenatal development and birth; Infancy and attachment; Cognitive and psychomotor development; Early and middle childhood; Play and education; Adolescence and psychopathology; Emerging and early adulthood; Middle and late adulthood; Relationships and personality development; Care and developmental interventions; Death, dying, grief and bereavement

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism

candidateDecisions.label: Clinical psychology and mental health care
Applied and transdisciplinary psychology: work, economics, law, politics and data science

analysis: The closest option integrates brain and behavioural foundations, comparative neurobiology, human language, perception, attention and higher cognitive functions. Pharmacology and physiology provide biological context. Epidemiology & Public Health replaces broad evolution to add observational designs, confounding and causal interpretation. It complements the experimental, multivariate and synthesis progression and does not stand in for specialist psychological methods. The programme connects psychopathology, health, development and assessment to a research and data spine. The societal option retains psychology and empirical methods while focusing on climate communication, misinformation, persuasive practice, rights, social movements, civil society and youth resilience. These provide substantive context for social influence and division. The applied option connects organisational behaviour and negotiation to behavioural economics, economic inference and consumer psychology, with legal and political context and data analysis. Criminal law provides context, not clinical or legal psychology practice. Clinical psychopathology and assessment, therapy approaches, pharmacology and health psychology were considered as a separate direction. Those courses are already in the closest plan; related epidemiology, ethics, qualitative methods and legal courses do not sustain separate diagnostic, treatment and interviewing depth. The three selected options differ by fourteen, thirteen and thirteen courses (105, 97.5 and 97.5 EC). Psycholinguistics moves to its only planned spring after the gateway, and the applied plan moves AI decision-making, criminal law and behavioural economics to available placements. The published research row distinguishes the small-group empirical project and UCR optional independent research. Year 3 thesis placement is unspecified in the EER, so no workload is invented.

alignment.rationale: Both introduce biological and social perspectives on behaviour. UCR emphasises brain and behaviour. Maastricht brings in a wider range of psychological perspectives.
Both study social cognition and group behaviour. Maastricht also examines personality and individual differences.
Both study cognitive, emotional and social development across the lifespan.
Both connect the brain to behaviour. UCR uses comparative neurobiology and laboratory methods. Maastricht also studies imaging and brain stimulation.
Both study memory and attention with experimental approaches. Maastricht also examines perception as prediction.
Both study how the brain guides action. UCR focuses on perception and motor control. Maastricht also studies motivation.
Maastricht offers a dedicated cognitive neuroscience methods module. UCR uses related methods within perception and cognition courses.
Both examine how drugs act. UCR covers pharmacology across body systems. Maastricht focuses on the biology of behaviour and psychoactive drugs.
Both examine questions about the mind. UCR focuses on philosophy of mind. Maastricht also studies computational models of cognition.
Both study psychological assessment and its ethical implications. UCR adds psychotherapy approaches. Maastricht also develops psychometric analysis.
Both examine biases, fallacies and the evaluation of claims. UCR focuses on misinformation and scientific credibility.
Both introduce research methods and statistics. UCR includes research design, surveys and analysis of variance.
Both study statistical models for experimental data. UCR uses regression, variance analysis and related methods.
Both develop programming in Python. UCR also covers object-oriented programming. Maastricht applies programming to examples from psychology.
Maastricht uses a supervised small-group project covering the empirical research cycle. UCR’s optional independent research sits outside the scheduled courses.
Both apply psychological research to societal problems. UCR focuses on youth radicalisation and resilience. Maastricht covers a broader range of problems and perspectives.
UCR develops academic writing, research literacy and civic engagement. Maastricht includes a programme of psychology-specific professional skills and portfolio work.
Maastricht develops psychology-specific professional communication and reflective practice.
Maastricht includes a third year of professional and life skills alongside a competency portfolio.
Maastricht students choose 24 EC of electives. Options include faculty courses or an approved external package.
